attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as the router between node2 (lan-a, opt1/vtnet1, 10.50.1.0/24) and node3 (lan-b, opt2/vtnet2, 10.50.2.0/24). Added exactly one pf pass rule (interface opt1, proto tcp, source opt1-net, destination opt2-net, port 8080/http-alt) via config.xml + configctl filter reload, leaving OPNsense's default-deny in place for every other flow between the two networks. Assigned static addresses/routes on node2 and node3's second NICs (persisted via systemd-networkd .network files) since they had no route to each other's subnet initially. Verified node2->node3:8080 succeeds (data delivered through the nc listener), while node2->node3:22, ICMP, and the reverse direction (node3->node2:8080) all remain refused. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for node1, node2, and node3, confirming a changed OS-native boot marker for each (FreeBSD kern.boottime for node1, /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id for node2/node3) and re-verifying full recovery of interfaces, routes, firewall rule, and the exact same pass/refuse behavior after each restart.
